WA-2025-HB2192.title: Updating the role of the Washington traffic safety commission in identifying the risk factors that lead to roadway fatalities.
WA-2025-HB2192.summary:
The Commission is categorized as a public health authority and tasked with promoting and protecting public health and safety. The Commission is tasked with:
• receiving crash reports, toxicology reports, and related investigation information from state and local law enforcement agencies;
• receiving driver licensing records from the DOL for motor vehicle collisions resulting in a fatality;
• reviewing traffic crashes resulting in the death of a pedestrian, bicyclist, or other active transportation users, and including members of the Council in these reviews; and
• presenting reports of reviews of traffic crashing resulting in the death of active transportation user to the Council.

A "public health authority" has the same meaning as in federal law, which includes in its definition a public agency to which a state has granted authority to be responsible for public health matters as part of its official mandate.

The Commission is authorized as a public health authority to collect health care information. This information is exempt from public inspection and copying and may only be used for purposes the Commission is authorized to carry out, including for anonymized reports on fatal or serious injury collisions and for providing these reports and underlying data to the University of Washington's Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation. The Commission may compile and link data, store information in a secure database, and perform statistical and epidemiological analyses to identify causes and trends in traffic fatalities.

The Commission may convene a fatality review committee, which may:
• review crash information; statutes, rules, policies, or ordinances related to the incidents; and any other relevant information;
• make recommendations on how to improve traffic fatality and serious injury data quality, and consult with local jurisdictions and law enforcement agencies on data quality improvement;
• obtain and examine medical records related to individuals involved in fatal traffic crashes that occur in Washington; and
• publish reports summarizing trends, contributing factors, and policy or program recommendations resulting from reviews.

Meetings of the fatality review committee are confidential and not subject to the Open Public Meetings Act. Discussions among participants of a fatality review committee during fatal crash review proceedings, and documents, prepared by the Commission, other than the final report of the committee, are inadmissible and may not be used in a civil or administrative proceeding, unless independent grounds for such review exist.

"Fatality review committee" means a group of subject matter experts and other members recruited and assembled by the Commission based on their traffic safety experience to review incidents involving the death of a person resulting from a collision involving a motor vehicle, whether on a roadway, at an intersection, along a sidewalk, or on a path contiguous with a roadway.

WA-2025-HB2505.title: Exempting certain former foster care providers from adult family home licensure.
WA-2025-HB2505.summary:
Exemptions from adult family home licensing requirements are created for certain individuals who have been licensed to operate a foster family home or approved for a child-specific license.

An exemption for individuals who hold or have held a license to operate a foster family home for at least three years applies when:

•
the individual had provided personal care services for the former foster youth in the individual's care for at least three years on the date they exited foster care;
• the only unrelated adults receiving care in the home are those former foster youth who have received personal care from the individual;
• there are no founded or substantiated findings against the individual by Child Protective Services or final substantiated findings by Adult Protective Services; and
• there are no pending or prior adverse licensing actions against the individual at the time the youth in their care exits the foster care system.

An exemption for individuals who are or have been approved for a child-specific license applies when:
• the only unrelated adults receiving personal care in the home are the former foster youth for whom the individual received the child-specific license;
• there are no founded or substantiated findings against the individual by Child Protective Services or final substantiated findings by Adult Protective Services; and
• there are no pending or prior adverse licensing actions against the individual at the time the youth in their care exits the foster care system.

WA-2025-SB6081.title: Protecting Washingtonians from invasion of privacy, including the unauthorized disclosure of sex designation information and historic sex designation changes in official government records.
WA-2025-SB6081.summary:
Department of Licensing Records .

The DOL is prohibited from displaying, transmitting, or otherwise making available any record or supporting documentation of a person's sex designation change unless the person provides consent for a specific purpose. Credentials and digital records issued after a change to a person's sex designation may not include any indicator that the person's sex designation has been changed, including credentials and digital records transmitted for purposes of voter registration and to WaTech in the DOL's annual transmission of its electronic data file on all drivers and identicard holders.

PRA Exemption. Exemptions under the PRA relating to driver's license and permit records are expanded to include any record or information used to prove sex designation when applying for, renewing, or making changes to a driver's license, instruction permit, or identicard. Further, any record pertaining to a confidential vehicle license plate, driver's license, or identicard that, alone or in combination with any other records, may reveal the sex designation of an individual performing an undercover or covert law enforcement, confidential public health work, public assistance fraud, or child support investigative activity, is exempt from disclosure under the PRA.

Disclosure of Records to Another Jurisdiction . Records and supporting documents contained in a person's Washington driver's record that include the person's sex designation change may not be shared with another jurisdiction that requests the driver's record unless the person gives consent for a specific purpose.

Vital Records .

Personal information collected from individuals who have requested a change to their sex designation in a vital record is exempt from disclosure under the PRA. Supporting documentation related to sex designation changes must be sealed by the state registrar and may not be disclosed, and any supporting documentation transferred to the State Archives related to sex designation changes may not be made publicly available.

The reasons for which the DOH may deny a request for vital statistics data or records are expanded to include a determination by the DOH that there is a reasonable possibility of the data being used to cause or enable harm or disenfranchisement; that its use could reasonably result in disparate impact on the data subject; or that otherwise fulfilling the request would not be in the public interest. The DOH is prohibited from releasing a certification of birth to any government agency or court for the same reasons.

Except for certifications and informational copies of vital records, all vital records, reports, supporting documentation, vital statistics, data, and information contained in these records that are maintained by the DOH are confidential and not subject to state or federal discovery, subpoenas, or other compulsory process.

WA-2025-HB2428.title: Preventing unintentional lapses and cancellations of life insurance policies.
WA-2025-HB2428.summary:
Required Notice of Lapse in Coverage. At least 30 days before the day on which coverage under an individual life insurance policy will lapse based on nonpayment of the premium, the insurer must send a written notice of possible termination of coverage to the policyholder at the policyholder's last known address and a third party designated on the account.

An insurer must obtain and, upon request, demonstrate proof of delivery for each such notice sent by the insurer. Proof of delivery may include records sufficient to show that notices are sent first-class mail using an intelligent mail barcode, or a certified mail receipt, read-receipt for electronic delivery, or tracking confirmation from a shipping service.

This notice requirement does not apply to group life insurance policies, life insurance policies for which payment of premium is due monthly or more frequently, or term life insurance policies that have a term of one year or less.

Disclosure Requirement Regarding Designating a Third Party. At the time of application for an individual life insurance policy delivered or issued for delivery in this state, an insurer must notify the applicant in writing of the applicant's right to designate a third party to receive notice of lapse or termination of the policy based on nonpayment of the premium.

An applicant may make the designation at the time of application for the policy, or at any time the policy is in force, by submitting a written notice to the insurer containing the name and address of the third-party designee.

The insurer must transmit a copy of a notice of lapse or termination of the policy based on nonpayment of the premium to the designated third party in addition to the transmission of the notice to the policyholder.

Duties and Liabilities. The act provides that the designation of the third party does not create or constitute acceptance of any duty or liability on the part of the third-party designee related to informing or not informing the policyholder or any other person about a notice received by the third-party designee; making a payment of any premium on behalf of the policyholder; compensating the policyholder, beneficiary, or any other person in relation to a lapse or cancellation of a life insurance policy; or taking any lawful action upon receiving a notice.

The designation also does not create or constitute acceptance of any liability on the part of the insurer as to the third-party designee related to a failure to send a notice.

Applicability. The above requirements apply to life insurance policies issued on or after January 1, 2027.
